710343543505.name: Washington Ave
710343543505.note: Washington Ave, MP 77.6 (operator milepost for the location). IDENTIFIED 2026-09-03 by knockdown timing, after the operator confirmed the two candidates: Oak Knoll Road MP 75.9 (42.72437427473365, -88.30633610470042) and Washington Ave MP 77.6 (42.748335706475466, -88.30382519746779), 1.66 mi apart by GPS against 1.70 by milepost. METHOD: a signal drops when a train passes it, so its knockdown time is a position fix. Interpolating 543505's own knockdown between S Burlington (72.8, four operator sightings) and S Midway (80.1), transits paired first so each measurement is one train: northbound MP 77.21 (n=76, IQR 75.78-77.57), southbound MP 77.73 (n=72, IQR 77.51-78.10), combined 77.47. Washington Ave is 0.13 mi from that, Oak Knoll Road 1.57 mi. Robust to the S Midway anchor: sweeping it 79.7 to 82.3 moves the answer 76.97 to 78.55 and it stays nearer Washington Ave at every value. CORROBORATION: the occupancy quadrature reports the block on each side, so its entry points are the NEIGHBOURING signals - measured S entry MP 75.8 (n=80) and N entry MP 79.9 (n=61), which is Oak Knoll 75.9 and S Midway 80.1 to within 0.1 and 0.2 mi. That brackets 77.6 and fits no other position. SECOND INDEPENDENT LINE - head arrangement, and it agrees. The operator confirms the two signals are MIRRORED. Oak Knoll: 3-light vertical facing south for northbound traffic, 3-light over 2-light facing north for southbound. Washington Ave: 3-light over 2-light facing south for northbound traffic, 3-light vertical facing north for southbound. So the multi-head face is on the SOUTH side at Washington Ave and on the NORTH side at Oak Knoll. This WIU's N-labelled head carries the diverging family - aspect 17 in 3201 frames, 13 in 718 - and its S-labelled head carries none. The N-labelled head is the SOUTH-FACING head: a head protects the block a train enters after reading it, so the head governing entry to the north block is the one a northbound reads, and V1 established the N-labelled field is restrictive whenever the north block is occupied. South-facing head multi-head = Washington Ave. ALSO NOT USED: location number 4350 interpolates to MP 75.9 between 4200=72.8 and 4550=80.1. That scale is nonlinear here - 4200 to 4250 is 0.022 mi/unit, 4250 to 4350 is 0.037, 4350 to 4550 is 0.0125 - so it cannot resolve 1.7 mi and its apparent support for Oak Knoll is an artifact. REJECTED: the external wiu-def repo names this 'Oakdale Road' and calls it the sole intermediate in the span. There are two, both operator-confirmed, and its own coordinate for 'Oakdale Rd' sits 76 ft from Oak Knoll Road - a different signal 1.65 mi from this one. The name is a corruption of Oak Knoll Road attached to the wrong wayside. OAK KNOLL ROAD IS NOT RECEIVED. Its WIUID must fall between 542505 (N Burlington) and 543505; a sweep of all 11 captures finds NO id in that range at all. The earlier lead 710343544328 (one junk frame, 2026-08-26) is numerically NORTH of this wayside, in a span the operator says holds no intermediate, so it is not Oak Knoll and should be treated as noise.

710343545505.name: S Midway
710343545505.note: Named 2026-08-31 by elimination on the operator's instruction, NOT by a sighting. ESTIMATED MP 78.9. Basis for the name: between S Burlington (542005) and S Vernon (549005) the archive contains exactly one well-received pair of adjacent 24-bit control points - this and 546005 - and the operator's siding list has exactly one siding in that stretch, Midway. The pair works its switches together: 19 of 21 reverse-switch windows coupled. Second leg, from track circuits rather than reception: across 22 meets this week a train enters at one of these two ends, occupies NO track circuit for the length of its hold - it is on siding track - and leaves at the other end while the opposing train runs the main past the flanking circuits at 543505 and 546505. COMPETING ESTIMATE: the 2026-08-09 operator series (MOVEMENT-20260809 sec 5, NB#1) interpolates this ID to about MP 88.4, 9.5 mi north of the estimate above. Both are estimates; sec 6.2 of that document offers the reconciliation - its MP readouts may be lagged relays. Unresolved. ESTIMATE METHOD: knockdown times chained north from S Burlington to S Vernon and scaled between those two operator-supplied mileposts. Accuracy where it can be checked: 0.6 mi at Oak Knoll Rd, 1.2-1.9 mi at the Midway ends. Treat as +/-2 mi. NOT a sighting.

710343565005.name: N Sussex
710343565005.note: CONTROL POINT WITH AN ELECTRIC LOCK on the switch - operator, 2026-09-03. NOT an intermediate in the sense this file uses the word, despite its [N,S] two-signal shape. Do not apply the intermediate convention to it. The ATCS block corroborates this independently and nobody had read it this way: 565005 is the ONLY plant on the sub with NO switch-machine keys at all - no NWK, no RWK, no SWCURRK - while carrying BOTH direction pairs of lock keys, NRELK/NREQK and SRELK/SREQK, plus 0LTK and LCK. Every power-operated control point here (552005, 553505, 557005, 562005, 567005, 568005) has NWK/RWK/SWCURRK and at most ONE rel/req pair. No switch machine to detect, and a release requestable from either direction, is exactly a hand-throw switch under electric lock. TRAILER [10:16] IS UNEXERCISED, NOT DEAD - and no bits have been discarded. It reads 000000 in 168,627 of 168,628 frames; the single exception (F7B4, 2026-08-25 09:00:13) flips three bits for one frame between identical neighbours 28 s and 8 s away with the signals unchanged, which is an RF bit error, not a lock cycle - a release persists for minutes. The lock was simply never requested during the archive window, which is ordinary for an industry lock. Those bits most likely carry lock state (request / release / time-out); they remain available in the trailer that decode_fields returns (wiu_decode.py:218) and wiu_decode emits (line 402). WATCH FOR the first sustained non-zero trailer here: that is a lock cycle, and it is what would let the field be declared with a known width. An `occ` field was appended on 2026-09-03 under the intermediate convention and REMOVED the same day - labelling lock state as occupancy would have reported 'Both occupied' permanently. The removal took the LABEL off, not the bits. Signals are fully live: 15/15 x91816, 15/7 x31775, 3/15 x27433, 15/8, 15/17, 15/13.

710343570505.name: Slinger
710343570505.note: 2sw+4sig CP on the Waukesha Sub between Allenton (north) and N Ackerville (south), with two WAMX connections. Serialized field roles, 24 bits fully consumed: sw1[0:2] sw2[2:4] S1N[4:9] S1R[9:14] N2N[14:19] N2R[19:24]. SW1 is the west/north switch (reverse route to WAMX-Horicon), SW2 the east/south switch (reverse route to WAMX-Milwaukee). S1* is the north-facing pair governing southbound moves, N2* the south-facing pair governing northbound; the N head of each pair reads with its switch Normal, the R head with it Reverse. Layout established 2026-08-26 over 3830 frames (rpi5-Util capture wiu_20260825-185319): the 1sw/3sig CP layout yields 0% in-vocabulary aspects here, this one 100%; all five switch 'I' reads sit between an N frame and an R frame. Operator ground truth the same day - a northbound had N2N Clear 12:59:32-13:05:24; S1R (WAMX-Horicon) showed Red over Green 13:10:08-13:25:08, its only non-STOP interval in the whole capture, with both switches Reverse; S1N held Yellow over Green 19:00:16-19:57:28. Head names and geography from the operator's track diagram. Was an auto-generated 3-switch stub before this.
